Hi Rajiv — thanks for the traffic sample, that helped. High level answers first; Karthik included a short technical proposal below with the sizing math. I'm also attaching a draft playbook so your procurement and SRE teams have something to iterate on (redwood-playbook-draft-v1.docx).

Summary:
- Baseline reserved slab sized to 95th percentile sustained QPS with a 1.2x safety buffer for typical steady-state.
- Transient burst (ephemeral slab) for short spikes: prewarmed pool + opportunistic transient nodes that can scale up to 2.5x baseline for windows up to 30 minutes.
- Autoscale cadence: aggressive up at 30s/60s (node prewarm hooks), conservative down at 5m/15m depending on session persistence.
- SLAs: We can commit to latency bands for the reserved slab (p50/p95/p99) in the SLA appendix; transient slab performance is best-effort but we will guarantee prioritized routing and fallback to a compatible quantized model variant when a transient hit affects latency.

Action items for CloudCore: please confirm target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and whether you want pre-arranged burst credit buckets (recommended for predictable spend).

On Wed, Apr 24, 2029 at 11:38 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary:
> - Baseline reserved slab sized to 95th percentile sustained QPS with a 1.2x safety buffer for typical steady-state.

Thanks — adding technical detail so your SREs can validate. I'm including a short capacity model (capacity_model.xlsx) as a worked example using your sample_traffic.csv. Key points:

1) Sizing baseline slab
- Compute 95th percentile sustained minute QPS across the sample window = Q95. Reserve nodes = ceil((Q95 * avg_token_cost) / tokens_per_node_per_minute). We typically recommend slab sized at Q95 * 1.2 to avoid frequent scale-ups.

2) Transient burst strategy (what you asked about)
- Transient pool = prewarmed instances (warm_buffer) + ephemeral instances (opportunistic) that can be provisioned within ~45-90s depending on region.
- Tranches: allow two tranche sizes: short burst (<=15m) up to 2x baseline; extended burst (<=60m) up to 2.5x baseline but with a grace-level pre-approval.
- Headroom guidance: for enterprise deals we propose a guaranteed headroom multiplier of 1.4x baseline in contract, with an additional discretionary transient multiplier of 0.5x invoked via burst credits.

3) Autoscale policy (ops-friendly)
- Scale-up rule: sustained 90th-percentile spikes over 30s window -> add N nodes (prewarmed first, then opportunistic).
- Scale-down rule: only downscale when 5m moving average < 0.85 * baseline for two consecutive 5m windows to avoid thrash.
- Eviction/priority: customer workloads are prioritized by route; lower-priority background jobs face graceful throttling and queued retry semantics.

4) Cost/credit model suggestion
- We recommend a committed monthly reserved slab fee + burst credit bucket (e.g., 500k token-equivalent credits) that consumes credits on opportunistic nodes. Overage rate shown in the attached playbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Rapid traffic colder-than-expected: mitigate with a small always-on prewarm (5% of baseline) and regional failover.
- Long sustained spikes: convert to temporary reserved slab increase with a 72-hour notice SLA to commit capacity.

I'll join a tech sync with your SREs if you want to walk through the spreadsheet — available Friday 10-12 PT.
